sources.title: Yvonne Choquet-Bruhat, Introduction to General Relativity, Black Holes, and Cosmology, Oxford University Press, open-access first edition (2023), Chapter IX, Relativistic fluids
sources.locator: Full 300-page PDF inspected. Chapter IX, printed §§IX.3–IX.4 and IX.13.1–IX.13.2, especially pp. 210–216 and 227–228: dust charge advection, perfect-fluid stress and balance, barotropic equations, charged-fluid current, zero-conductivity scope and the stated local hyperbolicity conditions.

source_review.read_extent: Complete relevant equations in §§IX.3 and IX.13.1–IX.13.2, printed pp. 210–211 and 227–228.
source_review.supports: The relativistic perfect-fluid stress, coupled Maxwell/Einstein formulation, convection current, charge continuity, charge-per-particle transport in the dust case, and the distinction between zero and finite conductivity.
source_review.limitations: The book uses its own units and signs and treats additional fluid variables and conductive branches. It does not specify this item's EOS-defined N normalization or its independent advected Z field; those are expressly adopted model choices here, not a claim that all fluids obey them.

source_review.read_extent: Complete statement and stated conditions of Theorem IX.13.1 in §IX.13.2, printed p. 228, together with the immediately preceding charged-fluid equations in §IX.13.1, pp. 227–228.
source_review.supports: The charged perfect-fluid equation family and the distinction between a stated hyperbolicity/causality regime and the local Cauchy conclusion under initial constraints.
source_review.limitations: The book's theorem uses its own equation-of-state variables, potential gauge and conventions. It does not establish the exact CP06 theorem or resolve the current draft CP01/CP02 suppliers.

source_review.read_extent: The EOS and sound-speed discussion in §§IX.4 and IX.13.2, printed pp. 212–216 and 228.
source_review.supports: A barotropic EOS is a model input and its derivative controls the fluid propagation/causality regime.
source_review.limitations: The exact p=w epsilon torus constraint calculation is performed locally in the example; this source supplies no such numerical-data example.
